newsitem.title: FRANCE: French industrialist, clock pioneer Fred Lip dies.
newsitem.headline: French industrialist, clock pioneer Fred Lip dies.

text.p: French industrialist and clock-making pioneer Fred Lip died at the weekend aged 91, radio France-Info said on Monday.
Born Fred Lipmann, he took over Montres Lip in Besancon, eastern France, in 1939. The firm had been owned by his family since 1865.

Building the firm into one of the largest of its kind in France, with 1,200 employees, he developed what he said was the world's first electric clock as well as the first assembly line for watches in France.

He pioneered workers' welfare programmes, instituting what was one of the first nurseries for children in a French factory but also clashed bitterly with trades unions, who accused him of being too authoritarian.
Lip began to sink under competition from Japanese quartz watches in the early 1970s, when his staff took over the factory and tried to institute workers' control.
A protracted labour conflict ensued which drew national attention and ended with the firm going out of business in 1973.
